title: fix(core)!: a banned user's credentials are refused while the ban holds, at every door
body:
Clause-②: yes (narrowing) — while a user's ban holds, a request authenticated by an API key that user owns is answered as a key that does not exist (the generic `401 UNAUTHENTICATED`), at every door that accepts a key. The widening half: `@objectstack/core` exports the one ban predicate, `isUserBanInForce` (with `USER_BAN_FIELDS` and the `UserBanFields` type).
Metadata-protocol: none
Skills-docs: updated here — `content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx` and `content/docs/permissions/administrator-guide.mdx` state what a ban holds; the dogfood pin `api-key-banned-owner.dogfood.test.ts` exercises it.

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么:用户被封禁期间,其名下的 API key 在所有接受 key 的入口(REST 数据读写、MCP 等)一律按"不存在的 key"拒绝(401);封禁带到期时间的,到期即恢复;key 本身不吊销。
- 为什么改:封禁本应管住该用户的全部凭据,登录与会话已被拒,key 要与之一致;同时把封禁判定收敛为一个共享谓词。
- 风险与回滚:每次 key 鉴权多一次按主键读 `sys_user`(实测约 0.65 ms);被封禁用户的集成会收到 401,属预期;回滚即还原本 PR。
- 先看:`packages/core/src/security/api-key.ts`(准入处新增的封禁判定段)、`packages/core/src/security/user-ban.ts`、`packages/qa/dogfood/test/api-key-banned-owner.dogfood.test.ts`。
- 两分钟验证:`pnpm --filter @objectstack/dogfood exec vitest run test/api-key-banned-owner.dogfood.test.ts`,预期 4/4 通过。
- 需要你做的:无,席位落地。另有一项不在本 PR 内、由你定夺:名下用户记录已不存在的 API key 是否仍予放行,本 PR 不作决定,该项由安全席位记在其待决清单上。

## What changes

- **The rule.** A ban holds every credential of the user. While a user's ban holds, an API key that user owns is refused where the key is resolved to its owner (the shared key-admission seam in `@objectstack/core`, which every key-accepting door uses), with the same answer a key that does not exist gets: the generic `401 UNAUTHENTICATED`, same code, same message, on the REST data door (read and write) and on the MCP door. A ban with an expiry stops binding once it expires, as sign-in does.
- **Not a revocation.** No key row is revoked or rewritten, and a refused key is not stamped as used. Lifting the ban (or its expiry passing) admits the same key again, still judged by its own lifecycle: a key left unused past the inactivity window during the ban answers as inactive.
- **One ban predicate.** `isUserBanInForce` (`packages/core/src/security/user-ban.ts`) mirrors the sign-in check (the ban flag; an expiry lifts it only once strictly past; an unreadable expiry does not lift it). plugin-auth's principal-session mint and agent-forward identity view now ask it instead of their own copies.
- **Order.** The key's own lifecycle (revoked / expired / inactive) still answers first; the ban is asked before the tenancy and account-posture questions.
- **One anonymous entry.** A key refused for its owner (a ban) or for the tenancy posture (no organization under `isolated`) resolves to the same entry as a key that does not exist, on every composition: the guest's grants on a face that serves the guest, nothing elsewhere, never a session. Both exits share one helper (`anonymousEntry`, `packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts`).
- **Failure mode.** An owner read that throws is the branded store outage (`503`), as a `sys_api_key` read that throws already is; a store with no `sys_user` table holds no ban.
- **Cost.** One primary-key read of `sys_user` (three columns) per key resolution. Nothing earlier on the admission path loads the user row. Measured on the showcase stack (shared box): 0.650 ms per read (N=1000) against 7.738 ms per key-authenticated `GET /data` (M=300).
- Docs: the ban entries in `authentication.mdx` and `administrator-guide.mdx` say what a ban holds. The **Ban User** confirmation and its agent-facing description (`sys_user.ban_user`) say the user's API keys are refused until the unban and work again after it; zh-CN / ja-JP / es-ES carried, en bundle regenerated (`node scripts/check-i18n-bundles.mjs --write`).
- Changeset: `.changeset/banned-user-credentials-refused.md` (`@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, patch, BREAKING narrowing banner, ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`).

## Tests

- `packages/core/src/security/api-key-banned-owner.test.ts` (18): the predicate table; the seam refuses a banned owner's key with no principal; reads the ban columns by id as the system; a timed ban binds until it expires and not after; nothing is written during the ban and lifting it admits the same key; lifecycle answers first; absent owner row keeps today's answer; owner read outage is the branded `503`; missing table holds no ban; `resolveAuthzContext` resolves the same context for a banned owner's key as for a made-up key, never falls through to a session sent beside the key; controls for a non-banned owner and for a session with no key; on a face that serves the guest, with a guest anchor that grants a set, a banned owner's key and an unknown key resolve the same entry (the guest's set, in the one organization).
- `packages/platform-objects/src/identity/action-confirm-one-dialog.test.ts`: the Ban User confirmation pin now carries the new sentence and asserts it names the API keys.
- `packages/qa/dogfood/test/api-key-banned-owner.dogfood.test.ts` (4, showcase + MCP): before the ban the key reads (200), writes (201) and opens an MCP session (200); while the ban holds every door answers the key exactly as it answers a made-up key (status, code, message, `WWW-Authenticate`), the refused write does not land, the ended session is 401, sign-in is `403 BANNED_USER`, and another member's key keeps working; after the unban the same key is served and the key row is not revoked; a 3-second timed ban binds before expiry and not after, with no sign-in in between.

## Acceptance notes

- A revoked key answers `403 API_KEY_REVOKED` by ruling (located lifecycle refusal), so it is distinguishable from a made-up key today; this PR matches the banned owner's key to the made-up key's `401`, not to the revoked key's answer.
- The refused-key path does not stamp `last_used_at`, so the inactivity window keeps running through a long ban; a key idle past the window when the ban is lifted answers `API_KEY_INACTIVE` (remedy: a new key).
- The ban flag is read whether or not better-auth's admin plugin is enabled; with the plugin off nothing writes the flag except a direct row write.
